classified.ifMissingWhatBreaks: ABSENT — no executing code anywhere compares a session's verification level against an intent's floor, and no executing code recomputes the floor at all. Concretely, once the pipeline is completed package by package and `widgets.runtime` flips: (1) There is no `v`. `GateContext` (src/widgets/gate.types.ts:77-86) carries only intentTokenHash, tenantId, principalProofHash, now, record and submission; `AuthenticatedUser` (src/common/authenticated-user.interface.ts:3-12) has no verification level; `verification_level`/`verificationLevel` appear nowhere in executable source. So a caller holding any valid, unexpired, unconsumed, principal- and tenant-matching token can submit it from ANY channel at ANY verification level — a COMMIT minted in a first-party authenticated context is actuatable from a bare Telegram chat-id channel. The two codes that would stop that, `NEEDS_SECOND_CHANNEL` and `HANDOFF_REQUIRED`, have ZERO occurrences in the repository; only the lowercase union members `needs_second_channel` / `handoff_required` exist, at src/widgets/gate.types.ts:40-41, with no producer. (2) There is no `f`. `verificationFloor()` exists only at src/widget-contract/verification-floor.ts:72, which is EXCLUDED from the production build (maya-saas-backend/tsconfig.build.json exclude list contains "src/widget-contract") and is not merely uncalled but unloadable: its transitive deps are `export declare` ambients with no runtime value (src/widget-contract/ambient.ts:11 maxLevel, :14 targetFloor, :18 C9_CAPABILITIES, :21 c9Registry, :24 actionCapabilityRegistry; src/widget-contract/tables.ts:142 WIDGET_CAPABILITY_POLICY). A Telegram inline button minted an hour ago under the old policy would still admit.
